answer: Sybil resistance rests on a proof-of-work puzzle keyed to a per-epoch cipher seed: each identity must submit a distinct nonce hashing under a target, so every extra sock identity costs the same compute as a real one and the attacker's marginal cost grows linearly with account count instead of vanishing like free signups. The seed also seals a public ledge of prior epochs, so a farm cannot fake history: a fresh account starts at the bottom of a ledger it can only climb by re-spending real work, while a legit one keeps an ember of credit that holds its rate up.
